title: Personal data; birth and family origins
description: Isabel Miller fills out a personal data sheet with Peggy Egland, recording her maiden name Boyer, her birth in Hawthorne, California in December 1951, and her family's return to Nez Perce, Idaho, when she was an infant.

title: Parents and siblings
description: Peggy describes her parents, Jeanette Johnson Boyer, a homemaker, and Robert Boyer, a lifelong farmer, both from Nez Perce. She names her sisters Donna and Phyllis and brothers Randy, Steve, Keith, Larry, and Stan, all younger than her.

title: Marriage, education and hobbies
description: Peggy gives details about her husband Nick, their October 1972 marriage in Moscow, her pre-veterinary studies at the University of Idaho, and her hobbies, jobs, and organizational memberships including sewing, swimming instruction, grain truck driving, and Alpha Zeta.

title: 4-H work; advantages of rural life
description: Peggy recounts her eight years of 4-H with sewing and animal projects and many ribbons. She discusses why she prefers rural life, comparing it with her experience living in Leavenworth while Nick was in the army, and what she did during that period.

title: Farm upbringing; chores and gender roles
description: Peggy describes growing up on the family wheat farm, the shared household chores among the children, and getting her first lamb for 4-H. She notes that girls lacked sports opportunities growing up because there were no coaches for girls' teams.

title: Decision to attend college; meeting and marrying Nick
description: Peggy explains how her father encouraged her to get an education and how she chose the University of Idaho and the pre-vet program. She describes meeting Nick at school, dating for a year and a half, and deciding to marry while he was home on leave from the army.

title: Family size; recreation and television
description: Peggy says she wants a smaller family than her parents' eight children and speculates that large families were simply the custom at the time. She describes family recreation growing up as mostly picnicking and her current viewing habits, including watching the news and The Waltons.

title: Daily routine; plans for work and settling
description: Peggy describes commuting to campus with Nick and visiting his family. She outlines her plan to study medical technology in case anything happened to Nick, her belief that women have equal opportunities in veterinary medicine, and her openness to settling wherever opportunities arise.

title: Equal partnership versus parents' marriage; church
description: Peggy contrasts her parents' traditional marriage, in which her father made the decisions and her mother stayed home, with her own equal partnership with Nick in housework and decisions. She also mentions that neither she nor Nick attends church.

title: Fairs; advice for farm wives; household decisions
description: Peggy confirms her fair ribbons and offers advice for a woman marrying a farmer without experience, saying she would need to appreciate what farm life offers. She describes how she and Nick divide household responsibilities such as cooking and car maintenance.

title: Reflections on army period and dependence
description: Peggy reflects on the unhappy months at Fort Leavenworth, her lack of common ground with other army wives, and how she depended entirely on Nick for companionship. She says she would not allow herself to become that dependent again and discusses her view that women have equal opportunities in college and jobs.

title: Choosing a career; lack of guidance
description: Peggy explains that she went to college unsure of her direction despite being an honor student, ruled out nursing and business, and settled on veterinary medicine after encouragement from a professor. She notes that her high school had no career counseling and that few classmates knew what they wanted to do.

title: Future plans and closing
description: Peggy confirms that Nick will graduate in a year and that she plans to add medical technology next year. Isabel Miller thanks her and explains the release form for using the interview in presentations.
